Resident employee, 2026: (1) Nonstatutory option (NSO): the spread at exercise (FMV - price) is wages - a taxable fringe benefit subject to the supplemental-wage rules (22% optional flat or aggregate; 37% on supplemental wages above 1,000,000), FICA and FUTA wages, timed at the actual exercise (transfer) date; W-2 boxes 1, 3 (to the SS base), 5 and box 12 code V. (2) ISO and ESPP options: no FICA or FUTA at grant, exercise or disposition; no FIT withholding required on a disqualifying disposition or on the ESPP discount at a qualifying disposition, but the ordinary income is W-2 box 1 wages. (3) Restricted stock (actual shares subject to forfeiture): FMV minus amount paid is wages when substantially vested (or at transfer with an 83(b) election). (4) RSU (legally binding right to receive shares in a future year): FICA and FUTA wages at the later of service performance and vesting (special timing rule, 26 CFR 31.3121(v)(2)-1 / 31.3306(r)(2)-1); FIT withholding when the shares are delivered (settlement) as supplemental wages. (5) 83(i) election (private company): FIT deferred up to 5 years and withheld at 37% when included; FICA/FUTA not deferred; W-2 codes GG/HH.

Nonresident alien employee, 2026: equity income is wages subject to graduated withholding as for residents, with the Pub. 15-T NRA add-on, except that no add-on applies when the payment is withheld at the 22% optional or 37% mandatory flat supplemental rate. Only the U.S.-source part is wages for U.S. withholding: compensation attributable to several years is sourced on a time basis (U.S. workdays / total workdays over the period to which it is attributable, facts and circumstances). FICA/FUTA follow the resident rules (NSO spread and RSU at vesting are FICA wages) unless the employee is exempt as an F-1/J-1/M-1/Q nonimmigrant. Reporting on Form W-2; Form 1042-S only for wages exempt under a treaty claimed on Form 8233.

Nonresident alien employee, 2026: taxable fringe benefits are wages subject to graduated FIT withholding. Added to regular wages for the payroll period, they are withheld with the Pub. 15-T NRA add-on; withheld separately at the 22% optional flat supplemental rate (37% above 1,000,000), no add-on applies. Noncash fringes may be treated as paid per pay period, quarter, half-year or year (at least annually). FICA and FUTA apply as for residents unless the employee is an F-1/J-1/M-1/Q nonimmigrant. Group-term life cost over 50,000: FICA wages, no FIT withholding and no FUTA required, W-2 boxes 1, 3, 5 and box 12 code C. Only U.S.-source fringes are wages for withholding: housing, education, local transportation (main job location), tax reimbursement (taxing jurisdiction), hazardous duty and moving (new main job location) are sourced geographically, other fringes on a time basis. Reported on Form W-2 (Form 1042-S only for treaty-exempt wages on Form 8233).
